title: People's Socialist Republic of Albania
capsule: The People's Socialist Republic of Albania (Republika Popullore Socialiste e Shqipërisë) was the Communist state established under Enver Hoxha, who led the Albanian partisans to victory over Axis occupation by November 1944 and ruled until his death in April 1985 — one of the longest personal dictatorships of the twentieth century. Hoxha broke with Yugoslavia in 1948, with the Soviet Union in 1961, and with China in 1978, leaving Albania in hermetic self-isolation enforced by an estimated 173,000 concrete bunkers constructed across the country. The regime imposed state atheism in 1967, closing all mosques and churches. Following Hoxha's death his successor Ramiz Alia oversaw a gradual opening that culminated in multi-party elections in March 1991 and the formal dissolution of the socialist republic.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. State boundaries are well defined for the entire period, coterminous with modern Albania; the polity is one of the best-documented Stalinist states.
